1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods — apply a downward bias correction of 1–3% for the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.

2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >35.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the 3–7 day window following a spike.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day history shows volatility, forecast should not drift too far from recent 7–14 day average; cap forecast deviation at ±2.5% of recent 7-day mean.

4. Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if true outcome shows strong downward trend after day 10, model should adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day starting from day 10.

5. Model underestimates volatility in late forecast period — if true outcome shows sudden upward movement after day 20, add 1–2% upward adjustment to forecast from day 20 onward.
